newsitem.title: UK: Salomon singles out reinsurers in 1997 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Salomon singles out reinsurers in 1997 outlook.

text.p: Salomon Brothers sees better prospects for reinsurers in 1997 than for property casualty companies and recommends General Re and Swiss Re in particular as being undervalued.

"Reinsurance growth prospects are superior to those of the primary market...The operating environment for property-casualty business in both the U.S. and most European markets is unexciting," Salomon said in a note on Monday.
Demand for reinsurance is strong in the current soft rating environment, while reinsurers' exposure to high frequency/low severity catastrophes has fallen.

The outlook for life insurers is more complicated, Salomon said, with growth prospects in areas such as southern Europe partly offset by growing pressure on profit margins from more cost conscious buyers.
These cost pressures will continue to fuel industry consolidation, it said, noting that Conseco is among the best placed to benefit from this trend.

In the property casualty market, Salomon singled out Zurich Insurance and Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group in its 1997 'Global Insurance Outlook'. "Comparative valuations suggest greater investment attractions among leading European insurers than their U.S. primary counterparts," the stockbroker said.
